from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Digital money faces the double-spending problem.",
            "Users send coins to multiple parties simultaneously.",
            "We need a decentralized way to ensure uniqueness."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Digital Ledger Problem", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create transaction visuals
        tx1 = Text("Tx: Alice -> Bob", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
        tx2 = Text("Tx: Alice -> Charlie", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
        tx_list = VGroup(tx1, tx2).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(tx_list, "B2", "D4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(tx1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(tx2))
        
        # Highlight double spend (red)
        red_box = SurroundingRectangle(tx_list, color=RED, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(red_box))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        trust_text = Text("Trust Problem", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(trust_text, "F3")
        self.play(Write(trust_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "SHA-256 acts as a digital fingerprint.",
            "Any input produces a fixed-size unique hash.",
            "Changing one bit completely alters the output."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Cryptographic Hash Functions", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        input_data = Text("Input Data", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        hash_box = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=2.0, color="#0000FF").set_fill("#0000FF", opacity=0.3)
        hash_text = Text("SHA-256", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF").move_to(hash_box.get_center())
        hash_func = VGroup(hash_box, hash_text)
        output_data = Text("Digital Fingerprint", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        
        # Position
        self.place_at_grid(input_data, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(hash_func, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(output_data, 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(input_data), FadeIn(hash_func), FadeIn(output_data))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Indicate(hash_func))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        # Visualizing the avalanche effect
        bit_change = Text("0 -> 1", font_size=18, color="#FF0000").next_to(input_data, UP)
        new_output = Text("A1B2... (Different)", font_size=20, color="#FF0000").next_to(output_data, DOWN)
        self.play(FadeIn(bit_change), ReplacementTransform(output_data.copy(), new_output))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Public-Key Cryptography: Digital Signatures", [
            "Digital signatures use Elliptic Curve Cryptography.",
            "Private keys sign; public keys verify.",
            "Only the key holder can generate signatures."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        private_key = Text("Private Key", color="#FFFFFF")
        public_key = Text("Public Key", color="#FFFFFF")
        message = Text("Message", color="#FFFFFF")
        signature = Text("Signature", color="#FFFFFF")
        valid_sign = Text("VALID", color="#00FF00")
        
        self.place_at_grid(private_key, "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(public_key, "B5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show Key pair
        self.play(FadeIn(private_key), FadeIn(public_key))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Sign and verify
        self.place_at_grid(message, "D2", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(signature, "D3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(message), Write(signature))
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Verify
        self.place_at_grid(valid_sign, "D5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(valid_sign))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Proof of Work: Mathematical Consensus", [
            "Miners compete to find a specific hash.",
            "The hash must start with many zeros.",
            "This process is like a lottery search."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Representing mathematical block
        block = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#FFFFFF")
        block_text = MathTex("H(Data + Nonce)", color="#FFFFFF").scale(0.8)
        puzzle = VGroup(block, block_text)
        self.place_at_grid(puzzle, 'B2')
        self.play(FadeIn(puzzle))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display zeros requirement
        zeros_req = Text("0000... (Prefix Req)", color="#FFFF00").scale(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(zeros_req, 'C5')
        self.play(Write(zeros_req))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Miner success
        success_text = Text("Nonce Found!", color="#00FF00").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(success_text, 'E3')
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(puzzle.copy(), success_text))
        self.play(Indicate(success_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Hashing creates a permanent chain of blocks.", "Signatures ensure transactions remain tamper-proof.", "This creates a secure, decentralized history."]
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Putting it Together", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        block = Square(color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        hash_tag = Text("Hash", font_size=20)
        signature = Star(color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5)
        signature_label = Text("Sig", font_size=20)
        
        ledger_base = VGroup(block, hash_tag, signature, signature_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(block, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(hash_tag, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(block), Write(hash_tag))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(signature, 'C4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(signature_label, 'C4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(signature), Write(signature_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        final_text = Text("Decentralized Trust", font_size=32, color="#0000FF")
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(final_text))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Mathematical Foundations of Bitcoin: Trust through Cryptography
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic interest in computer science

sections.title: Introduction: The Digital Ledger Problem
sections.content: Explain the double-spending problem. Use a simple visual of 'Alice sending a digital coin' to understand why we need a decentralized way to ensure coins aren't duplicated.
sections.example: Alice tries to send a digital image of a 10-dollar bill to Bob and Charlie simultaneously; the network must mathematically invalidate the second attempt.

sections.title: Cryptographic Hash Functions: The Digital Fingerprint
sections.content: Introduce SHA-256. Explain it as a one-way function: Input (any size) -> Hash Function -> Output (fixed size). Emphasize that even a 1-bit change in input completely changes the output (Avalanche Effect).
sections.example: Visualize a 'Magic Box' where you drop a document in; it spits out a unique, scrambled alphanumeric string. If you change a single comma in the document, the string changes entirely.

sections.title: Public-Key Cryptography: Digital Signatures
sections.content: Prerequisite: Modular arithmetic. Explain the Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) mechanism (y² = x³ + ax + b). The private key is a large random number; the public key is the result of point multiplication on the curve.
sections.example: A 'Robot Courier' uses a private key to sign a message. Bob uses the Robot's public key to verify that only the holder of the private key could have generated that unique signature.

sections.title: Proof of Work: Mathematical Consensus
sections.content: Explain how Bitcoin miners compete by finding a nonce that, when hashed with the block data, produces a hash value starting with a specific number of zeros. This is 'finding a needle in a haystack'.
sections.example: Imagine a flock of digital squirrels racing to guess a combination lock code. The first one to click the lock (solve the hash) gets to add the next block to the tree.

sections.title: Conclusion: Putting it Together
sections.content: Summarize how hashing links the blocks (blockchain) and digital signatures secure the transactions, creating a tamper-proof mathematical history.
sections.example: Think of a 'Digital LEGO Chain': Each brick is glued to the previous one by a hash, and only the person with the correct 'key' can add a new brick to the structure.
